Our Story · American Clothing Restoration

The Things the Fire Couldn't Take.

A home can be rebuilt. Furniture can be replaced. But what happens to the pieces of a life that can't simply be bought again?

Read our story ↓

Every piece has a past

To someone else, it's a garment. To you, it's a memory.

A wedding dress saved from a special day. A father's favorite jacket. A quilt passed down through generations. The everyday clothes that make a difficult morning feel a little more ordinary.

When fire, smoke, soot or water damages a home, the loss reaches far beyond the walls. In closets and drawers are belongings that carry stories no insurance form can fully describe.

And when everything feels uncertain, one question can mean so much: Can any of this be saved?

01 / Why we do this

Before you call something lost, give it a chance.

That is the belief at the heart of American Clothing Restoration. Based in Ephrata, Pennsylvania, our work centers on clothing and personal textiles affected by fire, flood, smoke, soot and water.

A damaged jacket may look like another item on an inventory. To the person who wore it, it may be the last reminder of a moment, a milestone or someone they love.

We see the damage. But we never forget the person behind the item.

02 / The work behind the care

Compassion has to be backed by craftsmanship.

Fire and water damage can affect fabrics in ways that aren't always visible. Different dyes, fibers and finishes respond differently to heat, moisture, residues and restoration methods.

That is why we evaluate each piece with care and make practical decisions about what can be restored. Some belongings can be recovered. Others, regrettably, cannot. We believe people deserve an honest answer, not an impossible promise.

When restoration is possible, returning a garment means returning something familiar to a life that has become unfamiliar.

“Every claim has a number. Every item has a description. But every family has a story.”

03 / What recovery feels like

Sometimes, hope comes back on a hanger.

A carefully restored dress. A familiar blanket. The clothes needed for work or school. None of these things can undo a disaster. Yet getting them back can mark a small, meaningful return to normal.

For Kendall Reinford and the American Clothing Restoration team, the purpose of textile restoration is grounded in that human side of recovery. It's why careful handling matters, even when the task looks ordinary.

What matters isn't simply the fabric. It's what that fabric means to the person waiting for it.

A reliable partner when it matters

For families. For adjusters. For restoration teams.

Behind every property claim are people trying to put their lives back together. We work directly with insurance adjusters, carriers and restoration contractors to make the textile portion of a loss easier to manage.

With itemized inventories, photographs, written estimates, Xactimate-based assignments, emergency essentials, storage and scheduled returns, and authorized direct carrier billing, our role is to bring practical coordination and clear documentation to an already complex process.

How we support professionals →

American Clothing Restoration · Our promise

We can't undo what happened. But we can help bring back what matters.

Not every item can be saved. Every item, however, deserves an honest assessment and respectful care. That's the promise behind our work, and the reason we do it.
